Found one of my reviews for Zombie Army Trilogy, so I'm going to copy/paste it here with a couple tweaks.

I bought this a while back when it was 60% off for £10, so the price was pretty good in my opinion. At just over £3 for each title in ZAT, it's decent bang-for-buck, considering they're each 5 levels long and remastered, with each level having a fair amount of playtime difficulty dependent. Although it looked like it was getting some criticism, so I thought I'd just throw my opinion in the spotlight.

The gameplay on the whole is pretty nice. You have your sniper - the extension of your arm - but you're also armed with your SMG for close quarter firefights and traps for ambushing heavies or an oncoming horde. The SMGs have been said to be overpowered, and it's been a while since I last played, but I think that balances out the fact that there's a fair chunk of gameplay that's not really sniper-viable, so I think it's more to help keep it fresh. To stop it getting repetitive.

I've also seen some people complain about about the kick being too powerful - basically, after kicking a zombie/small crowd, they stumble and usually drop to the floor, requiring either a spray of bullets to finish them off, or another kick. Whilst you could almost run through the game kicking everything you see, in a co-op game, I found it to be useful for staying in the fight when you're scrounging for ammo.

When you play the game, you'll probably think of Call of Duty Zombies. Whilst I understand this is the go-to comparison (I thought of it as well, too), I realised that it's probably a bit inaccurate, and a more representative example would be Mass Effect 3's Multiplayer. After killing so many, a bigger enemy comes to ruin the fun. Rinse and repeat. In Mass Effect 3, you also cannot swap your weapons - whereas in ZAT you can swap for weapons lying around or in safe rooms, which helps if you find yourself needing to improvise, want to spice things up, or made the wrong choice in the preparation screen. You don't feel limited by any stretch.

On the whole, it's an alright game. I don't think it's worth the full price, but I'd recommend grabbing it and heading on it with a couple friends over the Christmas/Holidays. However, what does need addressing in my opinion is; - some sort of mission maker, where you can design and create levels and have other people play them, like the Workshop. It would no doubt help to boost the lifetime of the game, as there's not much beyond what's already offered. - a blood on and off switch. I'm not too fussed about a lot of blood in general, but I occasionally found it kinda irritating, so I feel like an off switch would be nice, but that's just my preference. - Also, if I remember rightly, I don't think you can talk with a mic in game, and that you can only do text chat. They need to add this in. That said, friends typically use Skype/Teamspeak, so again, it's just a preference thing.

Probably something like a 6/10 overall. The graphics are nice, the gameplay holds up, but I think the inclusion of a mission maker/level editor would improve the game 110%.

What are your thoughts?
